sql:

FROM ops.zones z
WHERE z.LocationID NOT IN (SELECT t.RatecodeID FROM lake.trips t WHERE t.PULocationID = z.LocationID)

hypotheses.claim: NOT IN over a subquery forces a null-aware anti join, which is expensive. (matched: not in (select t.ratecodeid from lake.trips t where t.pulocationid = z.locationid) order b)

The inner HASH_JOIN (estimated 312,468 rows) joins the full trips scan with a delim scan of zones, creating a large hash table that is the primary CPU and memory cost; eliminating the nullable NOT IN could allow a direct anti-join without this intermediate.
The sequential scan of the trips table (495,833 rows) is the main I/O bottleneck; rewriting as NOT EXISTS or a LEFT JOIN ... IS NULL could enable predicate pushdown or index usage if available.

The outer HASH_JOIN with a COLUMN_DATA_SCAN (estimated 0 rows) indicates a failed decorrelation attempt due to the NOT IN nullability; removing the pattern would simplify the plan to a single LEFT_DELIM_JOIN.
